title: Field Lab Runbook for LLM Constraints (proto)
content:
Purpose
This is a compact, field-facing runbook for sellers + SEs to run short pilots when customers surface hard LLM constraints (latency, token budget, regulatory data path, on-prem restriction). It is intentionally prescriptive: scripted seller language, a 30–90 minute demo/run, immediate fallback triggers, and post-pilot telemetry checks. Design goal is speed-to-evidence for platform value while minimizing engineering lift.

Audience
- Sales Engineers (primary)
- Account Execs (secondary)
- Field Ops / Solutions Engineers (on-call for pilot days)
- Customer Success (handoff)

One-line pitch for the pilot
"Show measurable latency and cost improvements while preserving answer quality in a focused 60-minute lab with the customer's canonical prompt set."

Preflight checklist (30–120 min before pilot)
- Confirm customer sample prompts (5–20) and 10 representative documents/KB pages. If not available, use our placeholder set: pilot-samples/v1.
- Get consent for synthetic traffic: ask for a single IP range / short-lived token.
- Verify target SLOs with customer (e.g., p95 < 300ms for 64-token responses OR cost per thousand tokens < $X).
- Confirm which environment: hosted vs dedicated vs private. If private, confirm network ingress/egress window and contact SRE.
- Prepare two model configs: "fast" (aggressive batching, quantized variant) and "baseline" (customer's current model/latency).
- Load prompt set into Redwood Console as a pilot evaluation run.

30–60 minute field lab agenda (compact)
1) 0–5 min: Framing (AE)
  - Purpose: short experiments, concrete numbers, immediate next-step options.
  - Ask: what metric would make this pilot a success?
2) 5–15 min: Data & Prompts sanity check (SE)
  - Validate representative prompts, expected response style, and safety guardrails.
3) 15–35 min: Live runs (SE)
  - Run baseline config (3–5 queries) and capture p50/p95 latency, tokens, error counts.
  - Switch to "fast" config: enable prefix cache, continuous batching and quantized variant. Re-run same prompts.
4) 35–45 min: Analyze deltas (SE + AE)
  - Show per-prompt latency delta and token-cost delta.
  - Call out any quality regressions (use eval rubric: factuality, instruction-following, hallucination).
5) 45–60 min: Next steps & cleanup (AE)
  - If metrics meet success threshold: propose two-week proof-of-concept (POC) or reserved capacity estimation.
  - If quality gaps: propose targeted eval set and fallback policy (canary traffic split).

Technical runbook (commands / quick ops)
- Start baseline run: Console -> Pilots -> Run -> select profile baseline. Note: annotate run name with account and date.
- Capture logs: Console -> Telemetry -> Export CSV (latency_tokens_errors.csv).
- Switch route to fast variant: toggle quantization flag + enable prefix cache TTL=30s, batch window=20ms.
- If private deployment: run local health check script (scripts/private-healthcheck.sh) and confirm KV cache warm status.

Quick heuristics (what to look for)
- Latency: If p95 improves by <10% but p50 improves >25%, there may be batching mismatch; consider reducing batch window.
- Cost: token savings >15% is usually meaningful to procurement.
- Quality: If hallucination rate increases >5% absolute, halt rollout and mark as quality-failure.
- Errors: Any TLS or networking errors in private mode -> pause and call SRE.

Seller scripts (short, copy/paste)
- Opening (AE): "We’ll do a focused run to generate side-by-side numbers — latency at the 95th percentile and a rough per-thousand token cost estimate. If you like what you see, we’ll propose a short POC to validate at scale."
- If customer asks about accuracy risk: "We’ll run your canonical prompts and show the change in our eval rubric. We only recommend variants where the measured quality impact is within your tolerance; otherwise we use fallback routing."
- On timeboxed scope: "This lab is intentionally small: it’s about measurable evidence, not immediate production change. We’ll hand over all artifacts and a recommended next-step plan."

Fallback decision ladder (immediate actions during lab)
- Minor latency uplift (p95 +10–20ms) + no quality regression: keep fast config but reduce batch window.
- Major quality regression: revert to baseline model variant immediately, record the failing prompts and open ticket (JIRA-XXXX).
- Connectivity/private deploy error: stop, capture logs, and request SRE bridge.

Post-lab deliverables (within 24 hours)
- Short exec summary (1 page): p50/p95 baseline vs fast, token delta, top 3 failing prompts with annotations.
- Raw telemetry CSV + eval rubric results.
- Recommendation: POC scope (duration, target throughput, telemetry gates) and cost estimate (reserved vs hosted).

Metrics & reporting (what buyers care about)
- Latency p50/p90/p95 (ms) per prompt and aggregate
- Tokens per response average and distribution
- Cost delta (est. $/1k tokens or $/month at projected QPS)
- Quality regressions (count & severity) based on the eval rubric

Common objections and canned responses
- "We can’t risk accuracy loss": "We’ll run your exact prompts and show the empirical delta. If any regression appears, we keep traffic on the baseline and iterate on model selection/quantization profile."
- "We need on-prem only": "We can scope a private pilot window. Preflight includes a short healthcheck for network and a temporary agent—no long-term change required for the lab."
- "How is this cheaper than our current infra?": "Two levers: fewer tokens per response (prefix/KV cache) and faster tails (continuous batching + kernel optimizations) reduce per-call unit cost; we’ll quantify in the lab and map to your billable units."

Risk & escalation matrix
- Quality: tag prompts with severity and escalate to Applied ML (ticket tag: ML-QUAL).
- SLA/uptime: any errors affecting >5% of runs -> page SRE and pause pilot.
- Security: if customer requests data deletion mid-run, follow Private Deployments playbook (PD-ops-erase).

Playbook variants (short)
- Quick demo (15–30 min): 3 canonical prompts, baseline vs fast, high-level numbers only. Use when executive wants a fast check.
- Deep lab (2–3 hours): add 50 prompt set, throughput tests at target QPS, and waterfall quality review. Use when buyer needs procurement evidence.

Artifact templates (where to copy/paste)
- Exec summary template: [Header], Baseline vs Fast table, Recommendation, Next steps, Owner. (Console -> Templates -> pilot-exec-summary).
- Ticket template: "Account — Pilot — Date — Failing prompt — Evidence (CSV/console link)".

Next steps (owner assignments)
- AE: collect decision metric and schedule pilot (owner: AE).
- SE: configure pilot profile and run preflight checks (owner: SE).
- Field Ops: standby for escalation window and assist with private health checks (owner: Field Ops).

Open questions to refine this runbook
- Should we standardize two default quantization profiles (safe / aggressive) and surface them in Console presets?
- What threshold of token savings triggers automatic reserved capacity recommendation?
- Would a one-click artifact export (exec summary + telemetry) reduce post-lab friction?

Notes to self / TODOs
- Add a short slide deck (6 slides) version of this runbook for AE pitch.
- Create a copy of scripts/private-healthcheck.sh in Console templates.
- Liaise with Applied ML to publish two recommended quantization presets.

Version history
- v0.1 (2025-10-12) — initial concept and agenda.
- v0.2 (2026-02-15) — added heuristics, seller scripts, and escalation matrix.

End of runbook
